paper.title_en: Strange correlator and string order parameter for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases in 1+1d
paper.abstract_en: We construct strange correlators and string order parameters for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases (NISPTs) in 1+1d spin chains. These diagnostics and the entanglement spectrum are connected to the interface algebra between two NISPTs. To compare phases, we first use finite-depth circuits of locally symmetric gates to minimize the bond dimension of each matrix product state. The resulting action tensors determine local strange charged operators and the charge decorations of truncated symmetry operators. The strange correlator probes the representation of the interface algebra realized by the two states. Higher-dimensional irreducible components yield nontrivial strange charged operators. For the distinct phases studied here, we identify such operators with long-range strange correlations. The full interface algebra admits a one-dimensional representation precisely when the phases coincide. For an on-site symmetry with a symmetric product reference state, the dimensions of the irreducible representations of the interface algebra also constrain degeneracies in the entanglement spectrum. We use unitary Drinfeld twists of a finite-dimensional Hopf $C^*$-algebra $H$ to construct general fixed point $\mathrm{Rep}(H)$ SPTs, action tensors and string order parameters. Our examples include the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ NISPTs and intrinsically mixed $G\times\mathrm{Rep}(G)$ SPTs with explicit Hamiltonians for $G=S_3$. For the self-dual Hopf algebra $A_{12}$, we construct Hamiltonians and string order parameters for the two $\mathrm{Rep}(A_{12})$ SPT phases and evaluate a strange correlator between them. We also outline a geometric extension to higher dimensions.
